about: Our own tiledata and animdata records (cc-P26, F-8), and our worn-item animations (cc-P62, F-35), and our creature bodies (cc-P139, F-46: bodyAnims, a .vd each, into anim7 beside the worn items), and the winter decor records (cc-P34, F-22: OSI's statue 0x1224, animated fire pit 0x29FD, animated oven 0x462, tree 0xCCA and fireplace 0x45D give the flags; the statue adds Impassable; frame interval 2 as OSI's fire 0x19AB and campfire 0xDE3). Nothing here is copied from EA's files: every value is ours, and the tiledata values follow OSI's animated runestone 0xADBA 'Runestone01 Glow01' and OSI's earrings 0x1087 (flags, weight, layer and height read from the client's tiledata.mul; see SOURCE.txt). app\Play.ps1 writes the tiledata and animdata records into copies of the player's own tiledata.mul and animdata.mul, and gives each equipAnims body a Bodyconv.def line, in a copy of the player's own Bodyconv.def, that sends it to slot 'slot' of app\sl-anim7.bin (scripts\build-equip-anims.py). Change only together with registry.csv. cc-P50 (F-32), the chest mimic: flags and height follow OSI's wooden chest 0xE43 (Impassable | ArticleA, without Container, since the mimic is not a container); its idle loop adds Animation, interval 4; the two dead tiles are ArticleA only. cc-P237 (F-21), New Haven community art: carts as OSI's ore cart 0x1A82, the oil lantern as OSI's lantern 0x0A15 (without Wearable; its animdata is 0x0A15's steps and interval 6), railings as OSI's wooden banister 0x08AE, beams as OSI's wood supports 0x019C, the palisades as OSI's palisade 0x0221 and the tents as OSI's tent wall 0x01F0 (both without Damaging), the campfire as OSI's campfire 0x0DE3 (one frame: no Animation, no Damaging), the cage and meat rack ours (Impassable, heights 20 and 15); shard-migration notes/cc-P237-tools/records.py gives each value its source. cc-P236, Chase's satchel and guild bag icons (13184-13189): each copies the stock graphic it replaces, read from the client's tiledata.mul, and adds PartialHue (the icons hold exact grays, so tier hues tint only the leather): the satchels OSI's 0xA272 'Ore_Satchel_east' (Container, weight 3, height 1), the two bags OSI's bag 0xE76 (Container | ArticleA, weight 2, height 2). cc-P265, the guild hall decor packs (28016-28294): one record per piece on its base ID, each copying a named OSI tile (vat 0x1550, flask 0x182A, crystal balls 0xE2D/0xE2E, fire pit 0x29FD, brazier 0x19AA, moongate 0xF6C, wooden banister 0x08AE, tall ladder 0x2FDE, stone wall 0x001B) or the author's own recommendation (RedRooster's tanks and crystal ball, with his frame timings), plus Animation on every animated base; shard-migration notes/cc-P265-tools/decor.py gives each value its source. cc-P277 (P139-D6): the rideable dragons, bodies 2086 (red; its .vd is over the 5 MB rule, so it is kept outside git and bodyAnims 'outsideGit' names its source and SHA-256, which scripts\build-equip-anims.py copies in and checks) and 2087 (colorable), each with a mount item (28295, 28296) whose tiledata record is on the Mount layer (25) and names the body as its Animation, which is how TazUO draws a ridden mount (Item.GetGraphicForAnimation); flags Wearable as OSI's old mount items.
